"TempPro" and "iBBQ" are NOT advertised names.

device.model: TP9012, TP920, TP940, TP960/962/968 (TempSpike), TP980, TP426 (plain BLE GATT series)
device.name: ThermoPro TempSpike / TP9xx BBQ Thermometer
device.notes:
Extracted from com.thermopro.thermopro v1.21 (48MB, TempPro APKPure XAPK).
Decompiled: 14,930 classes. Package: cn.com.adsmart.wifibbq.
Adsmart is the OEM behind ThermoPro's connected devices.

TRANSPORT IS PLAIN BLE GATT — NOT BLE MESH. The app contains no mesh stack
(no/nordicsemi/android/ holds only ble/ + support/; no Mesh Proxy 0x1828,
no PB-GATT, no provisioning anywhere in the sources). Service 1086FFF0 is a
custom vendor service. Two independent RE efforts agree:
daniel-corbett/thermopro-cli calls it "a simple BLE notification-based
protocol", and Bluetooth-Devices/thermopro-ble decodes TempSpike probes
passively from advertisements with no connection at all. An earlier
revision of this spec describing BLE Mesh provisioning was fabricated.

WRITE FRAMING: commands to the FFF1 characteristic are wrapped as
0xAA | payload | checksum | 0xFF, where checksum = sum of the payload bytes
EXCLUDING the opcode byte, & 0xFF (TP9012Data.getIntCheckSum).
Notifications mirror this: 0xAA frame header at offset 0, opcode at
offset 1. TP920/TP25W/TP904-family devices additionally expect a fixed init
handshake write (starting 01 09 8a 7a ...) plus a timestamp-sync command
0x28 after connect (thermopro-cli create_handshake_command).

Eight device change-utility families are dispatched in the app
(MyBleManager.notificationDataCallback): TP9012, TP920, TP940, TP960,
TP962, TP968, TP980 and TP426 (infrared). The TempSpike line
(TP960/962/968 and TP970-973) is the current retail focus.

TEMPSPIKE PASSIVE MODE: TP96x/TP97x probes broadcast probe index, internal
and ambient temperatures (°F + 54 offset) and battery voltage in BLE
advertisement manufacturer data — fully decodable without connecting
(Bluetooth-Devices/thermopro-ble parser, actively maintained). This is the
cheapest integration path for those models and obviates most of the setup
below.

FIRMWARE: the v1.21 APK bundles an OTA image for the ASR560X BLE SoC
(res/raw/ast6s53_v25_ota.bin, version string app-2.5.0-20251011.1000,
archived in the research store) pushed to devices over BLE by
OTAUtil/OtaConfig — TempSpike-era hardware is ASR560X-based, not Nordic.

ThermoPro is rebranding to "TempPro" (announced ~April 2026; temppro.com);
the app already references both buythermopro.com and temppro.com.

credentials.notes: No credential protects the BLE link itself — any central can connect and exchange commands. TP980 (scan name TP980R, the app's "tempWifi" group) is a WiFi + BLE model: opcodes 0x80-0x84 perform wifiScan/wifiConnect/wifiCheck and cloud binding, returning the WiFi MAC, an 18-char device did and boundUser — so a WiFi passphrase IS involved for that family, and TP980W is sold as a Wi-Fi model. No TP980 cloud broker endpoint is identifiable from static code; the binding rides the device did.
stored_on_device: TP980 only: WiFi credentials + 18-char device id (did) / cloud binding (opcodes 0x50-0x54)

factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset button sequence was established from the app or any public source. Consult the model's manual rather than guessing.

methods.description: Scan for the advertised name (TP940R, TP980R, TP960R, Thermopro, SmartBBQ, ... per ScanConfig.java), connect, enable notifications on 1086FFF2-3343-4817-8BB2-B32206336CE8, and — on the TP920/TP25W/TP904 family — write the fixed handshake (01 09 8a 7a ...) plus timestamp sync (command 0x28) before issuing commands.

steps.action: Power the thermometer on; it advertises immediately.
Scan for the advertised name and the 1086FFF0 service (the 128-bit service UUID also appears in the device's own advertisement).
Connect, enable FFF2 notifications, and send the family handshake where required.
Exchange 0xAA-framed commands on FFF1 / notifications on FFF2 — or, on TempSpike models, just parse the advertisements.

setup.notes:
Plain BLE GATT: scan, connect, subscribe to FFF2 notifications, run the short init handshake where the family requires it, then exchange 0xAA-framed commands. There is no provisioning, no pairing and no mesh layer. For TempSpike TP96x/TP97x models even the connection is optional — temperatures and battery arrive passively in advertisements.
Confidence is medium: the flows are read from the decompiled app and two independent RE projects, but have not been run against a device here.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the thermometer to a BLE client: no keys, no pairing, no account. Switching controllers is scanning and connecting from the new one. (TP980 additionally holds WiFi credentials and a vendor-cloud binding for its uplink — that binding is between the device and the cloud, not the BLE client.)

device_families.description: Basic 2-probe BBQ thermometer (app code family — "TP9012" may be an internal/OEM designation; no retail page found)
4-probe (+ambient slot) BBQ thermometer with meat temperature settings
device_families.protocol_notes:
Per-probe push notifications (tempReturn opcodes 0x61/0x10, probe index
in byte 1) — there is NO polling state machine on this family; the
setTemp(0..3) sequential-probing flow belongs to TP980. Other opcodes:
0x02 unit, 0x04 alarm setting, 0x05 alarm close, 0x06 device close,
0x67 color.
device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: BCD: temp = (b1>>4)*100 + (b1&0x0F)*10 + (b2>>4) + (b2&0x0F)*0.1 °C; negative when the high nibble of b1 is 0x9 (subtract 1000). Disconnect sentinel 0xCC,0xCC → -999.0 (TP940ChangeUtils.getProTemp; the same BCD scheme appears in thermopro-cli decode_temperature). Shared by the TP25W/TP920/TP960 family.

device_families.description: Pro-grade 4-probe thermometer with history upload and WiFi uplink (TP980/TP980W sold as Wi-Fi + Bluetooth models)
device_families.protocol_notes:
History upload: multi-chunk transfer with a first frame (opcode 0x02)
and continuation frames, 6 bytes/record. Probe reading uses the
setTemp(0..3) / readNextProTemp sequential state machine
(TP980ChangeUtils — an earlier revision of this spec misattributed it
to TP940). Other opcodes: 0x11 temp return, 0x12 probe connect,
0x20 temp auto-return, 0x50-0x54 WiFi scan/connect/check plus cloud
binding (did, boundUser).
device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: IEEE 754 float32 read LITTLE-ENDIAN (Nordic Data.FORMAT_UINT32) at offsets 5/9/13 (tp980TempReturn). The wire value is °F with a +54 offset: convert via fToC(raw - 54) — the same fahrenheit_to_celsius(x - 54) the thermopro-ble parser applies for TP97x.

characteristics.description: Client → device command channel. Frames are wrapped 0xAA | payload | checksum | 0xFF (checksum = sum of payload bytes excluding the opcode byte, & 0xFF). This is a custom vendor service — NOT the BLE Mesh Proxy service (that would be 0x1828); there is no mesh anywhere in this product.
characteristics.name: Command Write

characteristics.description: Device → client notifications. Frames mirror the write side: 0xAA frame header at offset 0, opcode at offset 1, payload after that.
characteristics.name: Notification
